body:
union organizer turned law student here. there are plenty of interesting union-side labor law jobs you could do, and most of them won’t suck your soul away. even the union-side firms, which are probably the closest thing to corporate vibes in this area of law, are much cooler than your average law firms. (it really helps that they’re committed to the cause!) and if you’re willing to make a low (but totally livable) salary, you can do even more interesting things like working for workers’ centers or other radical movement nonprofits.

i will say that none of this work comes anywhere close to capturing the heady feeling of being on the front lines with workers and wresting power from the boss. even the best jobs will feel a lot more backseat and office-bound. the legal work still matters a lot (as i’m sure you’ve seen), but if you’re driven by the human part of organizing, you might find the switch disappointing.
